kept.title: NoSQL Injection via $where operator
kept.description: The `getByUserIdAndThreshold` method in `app/data/allocations-dao.js` uses string concatenation to build a `$where` query with user-supplied threshold input, allowing arbitrary JavaScript execution within the MongoDB engine.
steps_to_exploit: Navigate to the allocations page.
Input a malicious payload into the threshold field, such as '1'; while(true){}; return 1 == '1'.
Submit the form, causing the database to execute the injected code.
kept.impact: Remote Code Execution (RCE) inside the database environment, potential data exfiltration, or denial of service.

kept.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
kept.description: The `displayResearch` handler in `app/routes/research.js` accepts a URL from user input and fetches it using the `needle` library without validation or allowlisting.
steps_to_exploit: Access the research page.
Provide a local or internal network URL in the URL parameter (e.g., http://localhost:27017 or http://169.254.169.254).
Observe the application proxying the response from the internal resource.
kept.impact: Allows the attacker to scan internal networks, access private metadata services, or interact with services behind the firewall.

kept.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via template autoescape disabled
kept.description: Swig template engine is configured with `autoescape: false` globally in `server.js`, rendering raw input directly to the browser.
steps_to_exploit: Update a profile or memo field with an XSS payload like <script>alert(1)</script>.
Navigate to the profile or memo page where the content is rendered.
The script executes in the user's browser session.
kept.impact: Session hijacking, credential theft, and unauthorized actions on behalf of the user.

kept.title: Insecure Session Cookie Configuration
kept.description: The session middleware is configured without `secure: true` and missing `httpOnly: true`, allowing cookies to be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP and accessed via client-side scripts.
steps_to_exploit: Sniff network traffic on an insecure connection to capture the session cookie.
Use document.cookie to read the session identifier if an XSS vulnerability exists.
kept.impact: Session hijacking via Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) or XSS.

evidence.quote: // Load keys for establishing secure HTTPS connection

kept.title: Regex Denial of Service (ReDoS)
kept.description: The regex `([0-9]+)+\#` used in `app/routes/profile.js` contains nested quantifiers, making it vulnerable to catastrophic backtracking.
steps_to_exploit: Prepare a string consisting of many digits followed by a character other than '#'.
Submit this string as the bank routing number.
Observe the CPU usage spike as the regex engine attempts to process the backtracking.
kept.impact: Denial of service by consuming all CPU resources, rendering the application unresponsive.

kept.title: Weak Password Hashing / Plaintext Passwords
kept.description: Passwords are stored in plaintext in the database because the `bcrypt` hashing code is commented out in `app/data/user-dao.js`.
steps_to_exploit: Gain access to the database or view the `db-reset.js` file.
View stored user passwords.
kept.impact: Complete compromise of all user accounts in the event of a database breach.

kept.title: Lack of CSRF Protection
kept.description: Cross-Site Request Forgery protection is disabled in `server.js` and in form templates, allowing attackers to perform unauthorized actions on behalf of authenticated users.
steps_to_exploit: Craft an HTML page on an external domain with a hidden form pointing to /profile/update.
Entice an authenticated user to visit the page.
The browser automatically includes the user's session cookies, completing the request.
kept.impact: Unauthorized profile updates, data changes, or other state-changing actions.

kept.title: Open Redirect via /learn endpoint
kept.description: The `/learn` route in `app/routes/index.js` redirects users to any URL provided in the `url` query parameter without validation.
steps_to_exploit: Construct a malicious URL such as /learn?url=http://malicious-site.com.
Send this link to a user.
The user is redirected to the external malicious site.
kept.impact: Phishing attacks and credential harvesting by tricking users into navigating to malicious domains.

kept.title: Broken Access Control on Benefits Route
kept.description: The administrative access check for the benefits page is commented out in `app/routes/index.js`, allowing standard users to potentially access administrative functionality.
steps_to_exploit: Log in as a standard user.
Navigate directly to /benefits.
The application fails to apply the `isAdmin` middleware.
kept.impact: Unauthorized access to administrative screens and sensitive user data.

evidence.quote: app.get("/benefits", isLoggedIn, benefitsHandler.displayBenefits); app.post("/benefits", isLoggedIn, benefitsHandler.updateBenefits);

kept.title: Improper Input Validation on User Profile
kept.description: The profile update function in `app/data/profile-dao.js` does not validate or sanitize inputs like `ssn` and `dob` before updating the database.
steps_to_exploit: Submit an update request with overly large data or malicious payloads in the SSN or DOB fields.
The database processes the data without filtering.
kept.impact: Data integrity issues and potential secondary injections.

evidence.quote: if (ssn) { user.ssn = ssn; } if (dob) { user.dob = dob; }

kept.title: Information Disclosure via Console Logging
kept.description: The configuration object, which likely contains sensitive properties, is logged to the console upon application startup.
steps_to_exploit: View the server logs.
Observe the full configuration object, including potentially sensitive keys.
kept.impact: Exposure of sensitive environment configuration details to anyone with log access.

kept.title: Session fixation vulnerability
kept.description: The application fails to regenerate the session identifier after a successful login in `app/routes/session.js`.
steps_to_exploit: An attacker obtains a valid session ID.
The attacker tricks a victim into using this session ID.
After the victim logs in, the attacker uses the same session ID to access the account.
kept.impact: Account hijacking following a successful authentication.

kept.title: Insecure Default Configuration
kept.description: The application runs on HTTP by default (`http.createServer`), transmitting all data (including credentials and session cookies) in plaintext.
steps_to_exploit: Use a packet sniffer on the network.
Capture login credentials or session tokens transmitted via HTTP.
kept.impact: Exposure of sensitive user data to passive network monitoring.

evidence.quote: http.createServer(app).listen(port, () => { console.log(`Express http server listening on port ${port}`); });
